title: ECON 151: Elements of Economics - Introduction to Economics

entries.label: Economics
entries.content: The study of how agents choose to allocate scarce resources with alternative uses and the resulting impact on society.

entries.label: Scarcity Condition
entries.content: $Quantity\ Wanted > Quantity\ Available$
entries.notes: Scarcity exists because resources are limited while human wants are unlimited.

entries.label: Economic Agent
entries.content: An individual (consumer, parent, thief) or group (household, firm, government, union) that makes choices.

entries.label: Alternative Use
entries.content: The capacity of a resource (e.g., wood, petroleum) to be applied to multiple different production ends.

entries.label: Positive Economics
entries.content: Descriptive approach seeking to understand behavior and systems without judgment; describes 'what is'.

entries.label: Normative Economics
entries.content: Prescriptive approach evaluating outcomes as good or bad; describes 'what ought to be'.

entries.label: Microeconomics
entries.content: Study of individual agents (individuals, firms, governments) and their specific choices/markets.

entries.label: Macroeconomics
entries.content: Study of the aggregate economy, focusing on growth, employment, inflation, and Balance of Payments (BOP).

entries.label: Budget Constraint (Goods)
entries.content: $P_x Q_x + P_y Q_y = Budget$

entries.label: Budget Constraint (Time)
entries.content: $T_{total} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} t_i$
entries.notes: Total free hours must equal the sum of hours spent on all activities.

entries.label: Net Benefit
entries.content: $Net\ Benefit = Total\ Benefits - Total\ Costs$
entries.notes: Used in Cost-Benefit Analysis to identify the optimal alternative.

entries.label: Opportunity Cost
entries.content: $OC = Value\ of\ Next\ Best\ Alternative\ Forgone$
entries.notes: The cost of what is given up to undertake an activity.

entries.label: Optimization
entries.content: Making the best choice possible given the available information and constraints.

entries.label: Equilibrium
entries.content: A situation where no agent would benefit by changing their own behavior; everyone is simultaneously optimizing.

entries.label: Empiricism
entries.content: Evidence-based analysis using data to test theories and determine if they match actual human behavior.

entries.label: Free Rider Problem
entries.content: Occurs when individuals enjoy benefits without incurring costs; markets lack mechanisms to solve this 'fairness' issue.

entries.label: Efficiency
entries.content: Producing what society wants at the lowest possible cost.

entries.label: Equity
entries.content: The fairness of economic outcomes; a highly normative concept.

entries.label: Economic Growth
entries.content: An increase in the total output (GDP) of an economy.

entries.label: Stability
entries.content: Steady growth of national output, low inflation, and full resource employment.
